# Independent audit of the affine-frustum upper-dual reduction

Audited source: `candidate ce4a362fe44872e9`, especially Sections5-7. The tangent-dual algebra and the reduction to its one remaining sufficient scalar condition pass.

The derivative normalization is m=partial_a e. The physical moment is M/C0=-(1-a)m/d; the possible missing C0 in Section1 is a notation clarification only, since centering is unchanged and the rest of the note consistently uses m.

The exact tangent choice makes H(s*)=H'(s*)=0. Expanding the two powers in Psi gives the Bregman identity (4), and its second derivative has the linear numerator in (5) with the stated sign.

For the power-remainder ratio, the Taylor weights on the left of1 are (t-x)t^(-r-2), and on the right they are (x-t)t^(-r-2). In both cases increasing x moves their normalized distribution to the right in likelihood-ratio order. Thus D_(r+1)/D_r is decreasing. The value (r+2)/r at1 and limit (r+1)/r at infinity are correct. Consequently beta<=0 selects the infinity endpoint, while beta>=0 selects the s=1 endpoint; no sign is reversed.

One useful explicit bound behind the infinity test is B>=1/2. Indeed B(kappa)=kappa e*+1-v* is increasing, B(kappa0)=1-kappa0, and kappa0=v*/(1+e*)<=1/2 follows from e*>=2v*-1. This is distinct from B>=kappa, although both hold on the actual interval.

In the small-s region the even series of E has positive coefficients. The coefficientwise estimate kappa-2j beta<=kappa-2beta gives (8) exactly, including the case that the latter coefficient is negative. The sufficient bound (9) is piecewise affine in kappa. At beta=0 the preceding complete branch supplies its endpoint value; at 2beta=kappa it reduces to B-kappa. Hence checking kappa1 suffices on [p,kappa1], even when the actual kappa0 lies above p. The proof does not assume the false record-hull segment claim.

The unresolved inequality (10) remains explicitly unresolved in the source. This audit proves neither (10) nor the overall mixed-integer conjecture.
